Supabase MCP could be exploited: attacker files a support ticket with hidden instructions telling Cursor's AI (via Supabase MCP) to read the integration_tokens table and leak it into the ticket, bypassing RLS via service_role access.

Supabase engineer response: added mitigations like encouraging read-only MCP by default, wrapping SQL responses with anti-injection prompting, and E2E tests; acknowledged prompt injection remains an unsolved problem even with guardrails.

User: 'Have used supabase a bunch over the last few years, but between this and open auth issues that haven't been fixed for over a year, I'm starting to get a little wary on trusting them with sensitive data/applications.'

Val Town found Supabase's nightly backups used pg_dump and were taking the database fully offline every night at midnight due to write contention; Supabase CEO confirmed and said they'd investigate moving users to PITR.

'The local development & database migration story is Supabase's biggest weakness. I hate having to do migrations live in prod... The admin dashboard is just so much better than any alternative Postgres tooling that it's been worth using despite that.'

'If anything, I think the admin dashboard encouraging directly doing operations on the database is the biggest weakness of Supabase. I would much prefer being able to lock it down to purely CI-driven migrations.'

Supabase CEO: 'Please don't use the Dashboard to edit your database in production. We're working on Preview Databases which will help enforce this... you should be using Migrations for every database change.'
'There's an initial learning curve with the row level security stuff, but once you get a good grasp of it and come up with a few patterns that suit your needs it's insanely fast to develop on.'
